pr.title: Check inbox input for line breaks, long snoozes, and stray letters
pr.head: fb014a252b048aa09db8021412c7b7e250501ae6

summary: The inbox is where an agent leaves the person a question (which the person answers with a lettered choice, or dismisses) or a notice (which the person reads and dismisses). Each item is a JSON file in a per-session folder under Projector's state directory, and every change to it runs through project inbox. Two readers consume the store: project inbox watch, which prints one line per delivered answer, and the band, Projector's Claude Code plugin strip above the prompt, which lists items and runs the CLI when the person presses dismiss or snooze.
A review of project inbox found inputs it accepted and edge cases it handled badly, each of which lost or garbled what the person meant. This pull request closes them together:

• One-line answers. A recommendation, an option, and a typed --text answer must be one line, as the subject already had to be, because watch prints one line per event. A subject may not hold a tab, which would split list's columns, and ask refuses an option offered twice.
  • Bounded snoozes. snooze --for is capped at 1440 minutes, and a wake time after today names its day, as snoozed until tomorrow 02:13.
  • No stray letters. Only answer takes a reference with an answer letter such as #337.3.a; every other command refuses one rather than silently dropping it.
  • A distinct busy exit. Waiting out another command's lock now exits 75 rather than 65, the code the band reads as "resolved elsewhere".
  • Tolerant reads. list skips store folders that are not sessions, and every command treats a malformed item file the way list already did.
  • Consistent state. A dismissed question lists as dismissed, like a dismissed notice.

The pull request leaves out a fix for references that only one spelling finds, such as acme/app#337.3 for an item stored as #337.3; a follow-up replaces inbox references with plain per-session numbers.

cards.title: Exit codes the inbox uses
cards.html:
CodeMeaning
65Input refused, or the item is already resolved. The band treats it as "resolved elsewhere" and shows nothing.
66No such item, or the file is not an inbox item.
75New: another command held the session's lock for five seconds; run it again.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: The first Projector review, of 559f732, opened one finding: the band's ask and tell tools treated the new exit 75 as an outdated CLI and told the agent to run project upgrade. bf208f8 fixed it, and the review of fb014a2 verified the fix. fb014a2 also took the review's one suggestion: wake_time prints the raw timestamp of a snooze too far off to show, instead of crashing list.

groups.title: Checks in the inbox store
groups.kicker: What inbox.py accepts, refuses, and how it reads item files
intro: src/projector/inbox.py holds the store: it checks each new item, numbers it, and reads and rewrites item files under a per-session lock. This group tightens the checks and makes every read share one validation.

An item file is valid when it parses, its stored ref maps back to its own file name, and its kind is question or notice. list already skipped files that failed this test; show, the commands that change an item, and context crashed on them with a KeyError. The new item_in holds the test, and read_item raises ItemNotFound (exit 66) when it fails.

files.note: Adds the one-line, tab, duplicate-option, and snooze-cap checks; the InboxBusy exit 75; shared item validation; and a session-name filter in sessions().

checks.text: Under a lock held by another process, project inbox ask exits 75 with the retry message; checked by running it at this head. watch's deliver_pass still skips a busy claim, because InboxBusy subclasses InboxError.
list without --session called session_dir on every folder, which raises for a name that is not a session id. Filtering on the same SESSION pattern here keeps the two in step.
The cap check runs before the lock and the write, so a refused snooze changes nothing.

groups.title: The inbox command runner
groups.kicker: How cli.py parses references and prints an item's state
intro: run_inbox in src/projector/cli.py dispatches each project inbox subcommand. It now parses the reference once, before the dispatch, and refuses an answer letter on every command except answer. Before, dismiss q1.a printed dismissed q1, and the answer the person meant was lost.

item_state is the state column that list and show print. It now names the day of a snooze that ends after today, through wake_time, and prints dismissed for any dismissed item rather than only for a notice.

checks.text: Every caller that passes a reference still sends a bare one: the band's claim, delivered, reopen, dismiss, and snooze calls all pass ref, and only answerFromPrompt adds a letter, to answer. Checked by reading hooks/register.tsx.

files.note: Parses the reference once and refuses a stray letter; adds wake_time; merges the ask and tell branches.

checks.text: A snooze is now at most a day, so days is 0 or 1 for new snoozes. The dated fallback covers a spring-forward night, when 24 hours can end two calendar days later, and snoozes stored by an older release.
An older release could store a snoozedUntil past the year 9999, which datetime cannot represent. Printing the raw number keeps list and show working until the item is snoozed again.

groups.title: The band
groups.kicker: How the plugin strip reports a busy lock
intro: The band's act() runs dismiss or snooze when the person presses a button. It reads exit 65 as "resolved elsewhere", rereads the store, and shows nothing; any other failure shows a toast. With the lock timeout moved to 75, a press that meets a busy lock now shows a toast rather than vanishing. act() itself does not change; a new test pins the toast.

The band's ask and tell tools, which an agent calls to post an item, run the CLI through post. It passed exit 65 through as the CLI's message and added ; run project upgrade to any other failure, on the reasoning that an unknown code means an old CLI. It now passes 75 through too, so an agent that meets a busy lock is told to try again, not to reinstall Projector.

files.note: post passes exit 75 through without the upgrade hint.

checks.text: The ask and tell tool tests now check a 75 and expect the CLI's message alone; all 68 hook tests pass at fb014a2.

files.note: Comment wording only: "item" for "question" where either kind applies.

groups.title: Documentation
groups.kicker: The CLI reference and the inbox plan
intro: docs/cli.md documents the new refusals, the snooze cap and its tomorrow form, the letter rule, and exit 75 in the exit-code table. The inbox plan, which stays in-progress, records the same three decisions in its list of settled details.
